files.purpose: Status M, one-line churn. StdioProcess is the child-process wrapper that every stdio-framed provider or MCP server is launched through: it owns the Process plus its three Pipes, frames outgoing JSON as newline- or Content-Length-delimited bytes, and republishes parsed incoming JSON on an AsyncStream guarded by a single Mutex<State> (framer, error tail, exit status, exit waiters). The B2->B3 delta is exactly one added line, `var processIdentifier: Int32 { process.processIdentifier }` at :48, inserted immediately after the existing `var isRunning: Bool { process.isRunning }` at :47; every line from the old :48 onward shifts down by one. No other character in the file changed, confirmed by `git diff 1fbf81e6..HEAD -- DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift` showing a single `+` hunk line and by the file growing from 183 to 184 lines.
key_symbols: private struct State { framer, errorBuffer, exitStatus, exitWaiters } (:23-28)
var processIdentifier: Int32 { process.processIdentifier } (:48) -- NEW at B3
var errorTail: String (:51-53, was :50-52 at B2)
calls_into: Foundation.Process (executableURL/arguments/currentDirectoryURL/environment/standardInput/standardOutput/standardError, run(), terminate(), terminationHandler, isRunning, processIdentifier)
Darwin kill(pid, SIGKILL) in terminate()'s 3-second escalation (:127, was :126)
state_owned: framer: StdioFramer, errorBuffer: Data, exitStatus: Int32?, exitWaiters: [CheckedContinuation<Int32, Never>] -- all inside State, guarded by the single Mutex<state> (unchanged shape and semantics at B3, only shifted by the new :48 line)
side_effects: Spawns and owns a child OS process; writes to its stdin on a private serial writeQueue; reads its stdout/stderr via readabilityHandler callbacks; can SIGTERM then SIGKILL it
The new processIdentifier accessor itself has no side effect: it is a pure read-through to Process.processIdentifier, same as the pre-existing isRunning accessor
platform_assumptions: Foundation.Process / Pipe / FileHandle.readabilityHandler as the process and pipe abstraction

POSIX kill(pid, SIGKILL) targets the single child pid, not its process group (deliberately asymmetric with Shell.terminate, per PR-TERM-111's note), and processIdentifier now exposes that same pid outward
AsyncStream<JSONValue> as the delivery primitive; Mutex<State> (Swift Synchronization) as the single lock guarding all shared mutable state
feature_notes: The only behavioural surface added at B3 is a new public accessor, `processIdentifier: Int32`, mirroring the existing `isRunning: Bool` in position, visibility and implementation shape (both are one-line computed properties forwarding straight to the underlying `Process`). Before B3, StdioProcess kept `process` private and exposed no way for a caller to read the child's pid; every existing pid read in the codebase (Shell.swift:115, MCPHub.swift:372, StdioProcess's own terminate() at :127) reads `process.processIdentifier` on a `Process`/`Foundation.Process` value it already holds directly, not through a StdioProcess instance. A whole-tree grep of the B3 app target for `processIdentifier` found no external call site that reads the new `StdioProcess.processIdentifier` -- it is unused within this same commit (d70cff8fe, 'refactor: audit cleanups -- five bug fixes, shared MCP and provider code, layer rules restored'). It is still an observable, source-true addition to the type's public surface and must be carried into the port even though nothing yet calls it: dropping it would violate the no-omission rule, and a future caller (e.g. a diagnostics or provider-inspector view) could rely on it.

Every other line in the file is byte-identical to B2; all behaviour described by the existing StdioProcess records is unchanged, only their cited line numbers shift by +1 wherever the citation touches line 48 or later (isRunning's own citation, at exactly :47, does not move).
